rietkerk_2004.citation: Rietkerk, Dekker, Wassen, Verkroost, Bierkens (2004) A putative mechanism for bog patterning. American Naturalist 163(5):699-708.
rietkerk_2004.access: abstract/publisher paywalled; mechanism read from open-access reproductions below
rietkerk_2004.extracted_mechanism: scale-dependent feedback: vascular plants harvest nutrients advected by water flow; short-range facilitation (activator) plus long-range water/nutrient depletion (inhibitor) yields maze patterns on flat bog and string/ridge patterns transverse to flow on gradients.

eppinga_2008_2009.citation: Eppinga, de Ruiter, Wassen, Rietkerk (2009) Nutrients and Hydrology Indicate the Driving Mechanisms of Peatland Surface Patterning. American Naturalist 173(6):803-818.
eppinga_2008_2009.access: publisher paywalled; abstract confirms three pattern-forming mechanisms
eppinga_2008_2009.extracted_regime: three mechanisms (peat accumulation, water ponding, nutrient accumulation) produce similar surface patterning; ponding couples hollows/pools to inter-string troughs; different mechanism combinations give similar maze/string forms.

beguin_brunetti_kasparian_2019.citation: Beguin, Brunetti, Kasparian (2019) Quantitative analysis of self-organized patterns in ombrotrophic peatlands. Scientific Reports 9:1750.
beguin_brunetti_kasparian_2019.extracted: open-access implementation of the Rietkerk nutrient-accumulation Turing model. Activator = biomass (self-attracting short range, DB=2 m2/yr); inhibitor = fast-diffusing nutrient/water (DN=10 m2/yr) advected along hydraulic head; domain 256x256 m at 2 m resolution; nutrient input is the control parameter driving the sequence spots -> lines/labyrinth -> percolating branched network; clusters merge into linear and branched structures.
beguin_brunetti_kasparian_2019.regime_used: fast-inhibitor diffusion contrast (D_inhibitor/D_activator ~ 5) with downslope advection; 2 m process grid; 256 m output window matches the published domain scale.

korotkov_ilyasov_2026.citation: Ilyasov et al. (2026) UAS-LiDAR Mapping of Bog Microrelief. Drones 10(2):121.
korotkov_ilyasov_2026.extracted_regime_dimensions: ridge-hollow patterned bog: ridges oriented PERPENDICULAR to rainwater flow; configuration and spacing related to slope gradient; microtopographic (ridge/hollow) element dimensions ~10 to 100 m; ridges elevated 25-50 cm above hollows (regime magnitude, NOT used as Estonian amplitude).

model_selected.name: anisotropic two-field activator-inhibitor (Gray-Scott kinetics, along-flow anisotropic inhibitor diffusion)
model_selected.mechanism_class: scale-dependent ecohydrological feedback (Rietkerk 2004 / Eppinga 2008-2009): self-facilitating peat/vascular activator + fast-diffusing water/nutrient inhibitor -> Turing banding; slope anisotropy orients bands transverse to flow.

fields.V: activator: peat/vascular ridge-forming biomass (self-facilitating autocatalysis; slow diffusion D_v)
fields.U: inhibitor: plant-available water/nutrient substrate consumed by V (fast diffusion D_u >> D_v)

model_selected.anisotropy: strength = clamp(|grad dome|/slope_ref, 0, 1); dir2(U) is the second derivative of U along the downslope flow unit vector. Enhanced along-flow water/solute spreading orients Turing bands TRANSVERSE to flow (strings) where the dome is graded; strength->0 leaves an isotropic labyrinth/maze on the flat dome. This transfers the Rietkerk/Eppinga anisotropy regime by enhanced along-flow lateral transport rather than by destabilising advection.
model_selected.kinetics_choice: Gray-Scott is the canonical robust two-variable activator-inhibitor labyrinth/stripe former; the physically-literal extended-Klausmeier advection form leaves the homogeneous state Turing-stable except at impractically strong advection (verified on synthetic domains before freezing). The mechanism class (peat activator vs fast water/nutrient inhibitor with flow anisotropy) is unchanged; only the reaction kinetics are the robust Gray-Scott form.
model_selected.why_this_model: deterministically yields branch/merge/terminate string networks where the dome is graded and irregular labyrinths on the flat dome - exactly the demanded topology class - and is numerically stable under explicit float64 integration.
model_selected.validated_on_synthetic_before_freeze: flat domain -> labyrinth (junctions ~5700/km2, spacing CV ~0.63, pool coupling ~0.73, balanced ridge/lawn/hollow/pool); graded domain -> strings transverse to flow. Determinism confirmed (identical bytes across repeat runs).

topology.N_derivation: junction/termination floors derived from the published maze/string imagery (Beguin 2019 percolating branched networks; Rietkerk/Eppinga anastomosing strings; Korotkov 10-100 m ridge spacing). A genuine self-organized network at ~15-25 m wavelength produces junction densities well above 100/km2; the 40/km2 floor is a conservative discriminator that an evenly-spaced corrugation field (form-graph failure mode) fails.

pool_coupling.coupling_metric: fraction of pool-perimeter cells whose nearest string lies within the trough-membership radius (16 m ~ half the ~34 m string spacing observed in synthetic validation). A pool in an inter-string trough is bounded by a string within this radius; the form-graph's isolated sockets (no string within tens of metres) fail. Radius set pre-generation from the pattern's characteristic spacing, not tuned to the site result.
